intent: Test linux_configuration/scripts/single_use/fixes/lib/arch_perf_probes.sh to 100% line coverage and take it off the shell-coverage allowlist, sixth of the 16 untested fixes/lib libs.
scope: Non-goal: any change to arch_perf_probes.sh itself -- unlike the two libs before it, this one had no dead branch
changes: Added test_arch_perf_probes.sh covering collect_basics (a quiet machine, failed systemd units, frequent ACPI errors, a CPU-hungry Xorg, and the load-average threshold) and check_cpu_governor (all cores on performance, one core left on powersave, and no governor files at all).

Added test_arch_perf_probes_health.sh covering check_thermal_state (sensors present and clean, throttling messages excerpted, sensors absent), check_power_services (both daemons enabled, neither enabled, exactly one enabled), check_storage_health (healthy disk, disabled fstrim.timer, missing smartctl), and check_memory_pressure (heavy swap with RAM free, heavy swap with RAM exhausted, and a swapless machine).

The high-swap branch is reached by stubbing awk rather than /proc/meminfo, which the lib reads by absolute path: every meminfo read goes through awk, so the stub answers on the pattern being matched and execs the real awk for every other call. That closed lines 158-159, the only genuine test gap in the lib.

Added _t_stub_cat to lib_test_core.sh: the commonest stub shape is 'print this fixture file', and writing it inline forced every call site to embed a literal ${LIB_TEST_DEV} that must not expand at write time. Passing the fixture name as data removes that whole class of SC2016 with no suppression, and two earlier bluetooth test files were simplified onto it.

verification.evidence: arch_perf_probes (basics/governor): 16 passed; arch_perf_probes (health): 27 passed; both 0 failed. All 21 test files in the directory pass, so the five cleared libs and the eight pacman_hook_stall suites stay green after _t_stub_cat landed.
arch_perf_probes.sh: 93/93 lines = 100.00%, up from 91/93 = 97.85% before the check_memory_pressure swap branch was covered. No 'outside kcov's line set' lines reported.
arch_perf_probes.sh: 93/93 lines = 100.00%, exit code 0. Second matching run at the --min 100 bar.

verification.command: bash meta/scripts/check_shell_coverage.sh on arch_perf_probes.sh, arch_perf_report.sh and bt_audio.sh
verification.evidence: 'check_shell_coverage.sh: every checked shell library meets the coverage bar', exit 0, with the arch_perf_probes.sh allowlist line already removed so it had no exemption. The other two are included to confirm the libs cleared in c309c95f did not regress.

verification.command: shellcheck on every file in fixes/lib/tests
verification.evidence: All 21 test files plus the three harnesses lint clean, with no suppression added anywhere in this commit.

risks: check_cpu_governor and collect_basics read absolute paths (/sys/devices/system/cpu via find, /proc/loadavg) that have no environment override, so those cases are driven by stubbing the command the lib shells out to (find, getconf, ps, systemctl, journalctl). The load-average case additionally self-skips with an explicit note if this host's 1-minute load happens to sit below 1, so it cannot silently start asserting nothing.

The awk stub used for the swap cases execs /usr/bin/awk for any pattern it does not recognise. If the lib later reads a new /proc/meminfo field, the stub will fall through to the real awk and the fabricated figures will silently stop applying to that field rather than failing loudly.
rollback: git revert the commit; that restores the arch_perf_probes.sh allowlist line and deletes the two test files together.

After rollback, run bash linux_configuration/scripts/single_use/fixes/lib/tests/run_all.sh and confirm the remaining suites pass, then bash meta/scripts/check_shell_coverage.sh to confirm the gate is green with arch_perf_probes.sh exempt again.
